title: Delivery promotes the repo's project; the four duplicates are merged

story.i_want_to: have the repo's one project carry its knowledge, its channel and its delivery work
story.so_that: no repo ever needs a second project to start delivery, and today's four duplicates are gone

rationale: After US-52.1 a repo can hold one project, but a repo whose project is a kb scope still cannot take a pr or chg intake source: Intake.put_project/3 (lib/loopctl/intake.ex:323) only binds a :work project for those modes, which is exactly why the -delivery work projects were created. Enrolling delivery on the kb scope must promote it instead. Then the four duplicate pairs can be merged with US-52.2, and EscalationHandoffs no longer needs to find a repo channel apart from the story's own project (loopctl#1067 added that indirection only because the two differed).

acceptance_criteria.description: Intake.create_source/3 with mode pr or chg on an active :kb project of the tenant promotes it to kind :work in the source's transaction and binds the source to it.
The promotion writes one audit entry, action kind_promoted, entity the project, metadata from: kb, to: work and the source id.
A ledger source on a :kb project leaves its kind :kb.
A create_source refused for any other reason (chg_root_invalid, a changeset error, repo_has_project) leaves the project :kb: the promotion rolls back with the insert.

EscalationHandoffs posts an escalated story's handoff on the story's own project, with the anchor's repo part from that project's repo_url (its slug when it has none); the intake-source channel lookup and its work-project fallback are removed.

An open escalation handoff whose key names another repo part (a pre-merge handoff:chg-delivery:... moved onto chg by the merge) is closed and re-posted as the next generation under the project's repo part, as before.

docs/factory/runbooks/merge-duplicate-projects.md lists the four merges (chg-delivery into chg, ads_for_care-delivery into ads_for_care, claude-config-delivery into claude-config, infra-pilot into infra), the dry run and the checks to run after each, and records each run's result.

test_cases.name: a pr source on a kb scope promotes it (DataCase)
preconditions: human-anchored tenant; fixture(:project, %{tenant_id: t.id, kind: :kb, slug: "chg", repo_url: "git@github.com:mkreyman/chg.git"})
expected_results: {:ok, _}; the project is :work; one kind_promoted audit entry

test_cases.name: a ledger source leaves the kb scope as kb (DataCase)
preconditions: as TC-52.3.1; a chg root dispatch fixture
steps: create_source with mode ledger, change_events_secret and chg_root_dispatch_id

test_cases.name: a refused enrolment does not promote (DataCase)
steps: create_source with mode chg and a chg_root_dispatch_id naming nothing

test_cases.name: tenant isolation: another tenant's kb scope id is not found and not promoted (DataCase)
expected_results: a project_id error; B's scope still :kb

test_cases.name: the handoff is posted on the story's project under its repo name (DataCase)
expected_results: one post on the story's project, key handoff:chg:escalation-<id>-g1

test_cases.name: a handoff under the old repo part is moved to the new one (DataCase)
preconditions: as TC-52.3.5, with the project's slug chg-delivery and no repo_url; one sweep run
expected_results: g1 under chg-delivery closed; g2 under chg open

test_cases.name: the runbook exists and names the four pairs
expected_results: each pair's source and target slug and id, and a result line for each

technical_notes: Intake.create_source/3: lib/loopctl/intake.ex:259; put_project/3 at :323 checks Source.project_kinds/1 against the project's kind; the promotion goes in insert_source's transaction (the same place the audit entry is written) so a refused insert rolls it back.

The enrol route already requires role :user, RequireHumanAnchor and an unlineaged caller (lib/loopctl_web/controllers/intake_source_controller.ex:46-48), so promotion adds no new path into a work project.

EscalationHandoffs: channels/2, channel/5 and work_project/5 in lib/loopctl/delivery/escalation_handoffs.ex were added by #1068 to find the repo channel apart from the story's project; delete them, keep on_target?/3 and move/7 for the repo-part case, and keep tenant-wide latest/2.

The merges run through the merge_project tool (US-52.2) on LOOPCTL_USER_KEY: dry run, then the merge, then resolve_project({repo_url}) and channel_handoffs on the target. Project ids on 2026-11-19: chg eba0b4df / chg-delivery b5343742, ads_for_care 9fe72eaf / ads_for_care-delivery 329be116, claude-config 478f72ab / claude-config-delivery 0fc4aa3c, infra 0917eacf / infra-pilot 2b124878.
non_goals: A general 'promote' endpoint: delivery enrolment is the only path that needs a work project.
Changing claude-config's channel-claim gate: once a repo has one project it needs no change.

failure_modes.partition: n/a: the promotion and the enrolment are one transaction against loopctl's own database.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.3.1: the kind lives on the project row and changes only in the enrolment's transaction.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.3.4: a retried enrolment either meets the active-repo index on intake_sources and is refused with the project left as the first attempt left it, or succeeds once.
failure_modes.slow: n/a: no network call on these paths.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.3.5: the sweep runs in EscalationHandoffWorker every five minutes on any node, and reads everything it needs from the database.

definition_of_done: On production after the merges: list_projects shows no project named *-delivery or infra-pilot active, and resolve_project for each of the four repos returns a kind work project.
intake_source_list shows every active source's project_id equal to resolve_project of its repo_full_name.
